newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth urged to reinstate dividend.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth urged to reinstate dividend.

text.p: A group led by Greenway Partners L.P., a New York-based investment firm, on Monday said it submitted a proposal to Woolworth Corp seeking to reinstate the retailer's cash dividend on common stock.

The group, which holds a 6.0 percent stake in Woolworth, said it submitted the proposal on January 3 for consideration by the company's shareholders at the retailer's next annual meeting, scheduled to be held in June.
In making the proposal, the group said Woolworth's 83-year tradition of paying cash dividends ended April 1995, when the payout was eliminated.
A copy of the proposed shareholder resolution was attached to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
"Woolworth today is a far stronger company," the group said In seeking the resumption of the dividend payment.
It said that "even a nominal one of 10 or 12 cents per quarter will show the market that the management of Woolworth has confidence in the strength of the turnaround."
In addition, the group said, reinstating the dividend "would increase the universe of potential purchasers of Woolworth common stock."

The group said it still believed Woolworth would do even better if its Foot Locker unit were spun off as a separate public company, it said. The group had sponsored a resolution at last year's annual meeting seeking the spin-off.
The group said it held 8,071,922 Woolworth shares, including its most recent purchase of 40,000 shares at $11.125 a share or $446,000.
